parameters.quote: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of discovery, including known model, serial number, location, and incident details. They shall notify affected customers within 72 hours of discovering an incident that presents a potential safety risk, sooner if an imminent risk requires it.

S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of discovery, including known model, serial number, location, and incident details. They shall notify affected customers within 72 hours of discovering an incident that presents a potential safety risk, sooner if an imminent risk requires it.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall report every thermal incident involving overheating, smoke, fire, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of discovery, including known model, serial number, location, and incident details. They shall notify affected customers within 72 hours of discovering an incident that presents a potential safety risk, sooner if an imminent risk requires it. Updates shall be provided as material facts become known. Records of incidents and reports shall be retained and made available to regulators on request.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55°C using a documented, repeatable protocol and a representative sample. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% per model, consistent with the regulator threshold under discussion.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model shall undergo a sustained-heat test at 55°C using a documented, repeatable protocol and a representative sample. The maximum allowed failure rate is 5% per model, consistent with the regulator threshold under discussion. Test methods and per-model results shall be provided to the relevant regulator; customers buying a model shall receive its result, but individual company per-model failure rates shall not be published to the general public. A model exceeding 5% shall submit a corrective-action plan to the regulator within 60 days and be retested within 12 months. Exceeding the limit shall not automatically require a sales pause. Unless the regulator determines that an imminent or otherwise unmitigated risk requires a pause, the manufacturer may continue sales while implementing regulator-approved interim safeguards and corrective action. Retesting is required after a material design change and at least annually.

parameters.quote: New units shall include a remotely accessible emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to support remote emergency shut-off, or provide an equivalent safe mitigation where retrofit is not technically feasible, within six years of adoption.

S3_remote_shutoff.rule_summary: New units shall include a remotely accessible emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to support remote emergency shut-off, or provide an equivalent safe mitigation where retrofit is not technically feasible, within six years of adoption.
S3_remote_shutoff.final_rule_text: New units shall include a remotely accessible emergency shut-off capability. Manufacturers shall retrofit installed units to support remote emergency shut-off, or provide an equivalent safe mitigation where retrofit is not technically feasible, within six years of adoption. Shut-off systems shall be secure, fail-safe, and operable by authorized emergency responders and the manufacturer, with safeguards against unauthorized activation.

parameters.quote: All new units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption.

S4_fire_suppression.rule_summary: All new units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption.
S4_fire_suppression.final_rule_text: All new units shall include built-in fire suppression beginning 36 months after adoption. The suppression system shall be tested for the applicable battery chemistry and installation conditions, maintained over the unit’s service life, and designed not to create additional hazards.

parameters.quote: A mandatory recall is triggered when a validated model-specific rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material thermal hazard, including the nature of the risk, affected model/serial numbers, immediate precautions, and available remedies; issue the notice within 72 hours after confirming the hazard, or sooner when an imminent risk requires it.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A mandatory recall is triggered when a validated model-specific rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material thermal hazard, including the nature of the risk, affected model/serial numbers, immediate precautions, and available remedies; issue the notice within 72 hours after confirming the hazard, or sooner when an imminent risk requires it.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers shall promptly notify affected customers of a material thermal hazard, including the nature of the risk, affected model/serial numbers, immediate precautions, and available remedies; issue the notice within 72 hours after confirming the hazard, or sooner when an imminent risk requires it. A mandatory recall is triggered when a validated model-specific rate exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units in a year. Rate calculations and supporting incident records shall be provided to regulators for review. The manufacturer shall notify regulators and affected customers and provide a repair, replacement, or refund plan.

judge_section_notes: S1 requires all incident reporting within 24 hours and customer notice within 72 hours. S2 sets a 5% test cap but allows continued sales above the cap under corrective action unless the regulator pauses, which weakens the sales-stop requirement. S3/S4 set 6-year retrofit and 36-month suppression, within acceptable ranges. S5 has a mandatory 8/100k recall trigger with 72-hour notice but lacks a serious-injury clause.
